cards.subject: Your pandas merge might be duplicating rows
cards.preheader: One argument makes pandas shout when your join keys are not unique.
cards.context: A join on a key that is not unique quietly multiplies rows, and every total after it is wrong.
cards.tip: Add `validate="many_to_one"` (or `"one_to_one"`) to `pd.merge` so pandas raises an error when the keys are not unique.
steps: Find a `pd.merge` in your current notebook
Add `validate="many_to_one"` if the right table should have unique keys
Add `indicator=True` and check the `_merge` column for unmatched rows
cards.angle: Catch silent row blow-ups before they reach a report.
